land.text: Guzana (Tell Halaf) and its surrounding area on the Khabur

successors.note: "In 808 BCE, the city and its surrounding area was reduced to a province of the Assyrian Empire" (Tell Halaf page).

capitals.name: Guzana (Tell Halaf)
capitals.note: Coordinates 36 49 36 N 40 02 23 E from the page. "In the 10th century BCE, the rulers of the small Aramaean kingdom Bit Bahiani took their seat in Tell Halaf, re-founded as Guzana or Gozan"; the seat before the 10th century is not on the pages.

correction.text: Guzana (Tell Halaf) and the Khabur valley round it

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -1200..-809: no Cliopatria shape. The page puts the capital in "the fertile valley of the Khabur River" and gives no frontier; "By the end of the 9th century, it was a famous Syro-Hittite state". Drawn as a 60 km circle at Guzana (my reading).

ledger.note: c. 1200 BC: Bit Bahiani is established. The infobox: "independent Aramean city-state kingdom (c. 1200 - 808 BC)", establishment c. 1200 BC; the page gives no founding event. The Tell Halaf page has the rulers seated at Guzana only from the 10th century. The land is my reading.

808 BC: Bit Bahiani becomes an Assyrian province. "In 808 BCE, the city and its surrounding area was reduced to a province of the Assyrian Empire" (Tell Halaf); the Bit Bahiani infobox: disestablished 808 BC, successor the Neo-Assyrian Empire. Mirrors the neo-assyrian-empire gain; the tribute from 894 is its vassal_start/vassal_end pair.

wars.name: Assyrian reduction of Guzana to a province
wars.outcome: Adad-nirari II recorded the site as a tributary Aramaean city-state in 894; in 808 it was reduced to a province.
wars.note: The 894 sentence carries a citation-needed tag on the page, and the page names no Assyrian campaign.

certainty.note: No frontier on the pages; the state is a circle at its capital. The Bit Bahiani page names five kings and four governors without dates.

sources.title: Tell Halaf
sources.note: 10th century seat at Guzana; Kapara's hilani; 894 BC tributary city-state of Adad-nirari II; 808 BC reduced to an Assyrian province; coordinates; Khabur valley.

sources.title: Bit Bahiani
sources.note: Independent Aramean city-state kingdom c. 1200-808 BC (infobox), capital Guzana (Tell Halaf), King Kapara; "at least five kings and four governors". Thin.

notes:
SCOPE. Aramean state of the Jazira on the Khabur; Cliopatria lacks it (cliopatria_names empty). Two pages only, both thin: Bit Bahiani gives the infobox dates, Kapara and the capital; Tell Halaf gives the 10th-century seat, 894 and 808. Khabur, Harran and Balikh limits, wars and tribute are not on either page.
MIRRORS. neo-assyrian-empire carries vassal_start (-894, counterpart bit-bahiani) and vassal_end/gain (-808). Kapara has no dates on the pages, so no rulers list.
DISAGREEMENT. The infobox (c. 1200) vs "In the 10th century BCE ... took their seat" at Guzana: the c. 1200 start is the infobox's, the capital is dated only from the 10th century.
Gazetteer names missing: Guzana (Tell Halaf, coordinates from the page).
